items.expected-result: `ai-raccoon settings model threads <n>` round trips (set, show, list), and doctor/logs show the ORT intra-op thread count taking effect.
items.command: settings model threads 3 ; settings model list ; serve --restart (to pick up the new setting) ; a memory_search to force embedding-session construction ; grep the server log for anything thread/session/onnx-related ; doctor
items.evidence: set -> 'embedding threads set to 3; takes effect on the next server restart'. list -> 'threads: 3' (round-tripped correctly). After --restart and a live memory_search (which succeeded, proving the ONNX session built without error using IntraOpNumThreads=3): grep -in 'thread|onnx|session' across the full server log -> ZERO matches. `doctor` output has no threads line at all (only checks schema shape, encryption key, and the code engine). Source-level: OnnxEmbeddingGenerator.IntraOpThreads is a public property but is never logged anywhere (grep confirms zero call sites logging it); EmbeddingService.CreateLocal reads and resolves the setting but never logs the resolved value either -- only EmbeddingService.Log.InvalidThreadsSetting (EventId 419, Warning) exists, firing only for a GARBAGE value, never for a valid one.
items.observed-result: The round-trip (CLI set -> CLI list) works correctly and the session construction does not error with a non-default thread count, so the setting IS being consumed by ONNX (a wrong or ignored value would still succeed silently, so this is not proof of correct application, only proof of no crash). But there is genuinely no doctor output and no log line anywhere -- at any log level reachable through this build's supported configuration surface -- that confirms the resolved thread count actually took effect. This is a real observability gap against the explicit ask.
items.acceptance-reason: Accepted as a known, tracked defect: filed as GitHub issue #522 (https://github.com/Arasz/ai-raccoon/issues/522) rather than a checklist regression to fix in this run. The round-trip half of the item (set/show/list) passes cleanly; the 'doctor/logs show it took effect' half genuinely does not exist in this build -- confirmed by exhaustive grep of both the doctor command's own source and every log line this run produced, not by absence of effort to find it.

items.expected-result: `ai-raccoon settings maintenance embed-rows-per-run <n>`: set 7 -> list shows 7. set 0, "", 5000 -> exit 1 with the positive/at-most-4096 message and nothing written.
items.command: settings maintenance embed-rows-per-run 7 ; settings maintenance list ; embed-rows-per-run 0 ; embed-rows-per-run "" ; embed-rows-per-run 5000 ; settings maintenance list again
items.evidence: set 7 -> 'embed rows per run: 7'. list -> 'embed rows per run: 7' (round-tripped). set 0 -> exit 15 (this build's InvalidArgument code, not literal 1 -- see note), 'ai-raccoon: embed rows per run must be a positive integer, at most 4096'. set "" -> same exit code, same message. set 5000 -> same exit code, same message. list afterward -> still 'embed rows per run: 7' -- none of the three rejected calls wrote anything.
items.observed-result: Round trip correct; all three invalid inputs rejected with the exact positive/at-most-4096 message and confirmed no write occurred (re-read shows the value unchanged).
items.acceptance-reason: Note: the exit code for a rejected value is 15 (this build's ExitCode.InvalidArgument), not the literal '1' named in the item's phrasing -- the item's own template sibling ('cli-exit-codes-nobank-and-settings-error') documents 15 as the usage-error code family, so this is consistent internal behavior, not a discrepancy worth flagging as a defect; recorded here for precision.

items.expected-result: Ingest a small directory with both markdown and .cs files into a scratch bank with the code model active, then prove both corpora drain to embedded without inline embedding (via memory_embed_pending/memory_stats/doctor or the server log's EventIds 1002/1003 'drain pass'; 1006 must NOT fire with a valid setting), and that with embed-rows-per-run=7 a single drain pass embeds exactly 7 rows.
items.command: root-code: code engine already active (from item 16) ; memory_ingest_directory (README.md + TideSampler.cs, code engine active) ; doctor (pending:0 for both corpora) ; separately: 10 fresh .cs files, embed-rows-per-run=7, memory_ingest_directory (single directory-walk write, one signal per corpus) ; server log grep for EmbedDrainService[1002/1003/1006]
items.evidence: Mixed-corpus ingest with code engine active: doctor showed 'code rows pending: 0' immediately after ingest (both README.md's memory chunk and TideSampler.cs's code chunk drained without ever calling memory_embed_pending). Server log (once flushed on clean shutdown): 'EmbedDrainService[1003] Embed drain pass finished for Code: 1 row(s)' and 'Embed drain pass finished for Memory: 1 row(s)' -- both corpora, both via the async drain, zero inline-embed code path (confirmed by source: FileIngestor no longer holds an IEntryEmbedder reference at all, per PR #518's own commit message). embed-rows-per-run=7 test: 10 pending code rows created in one directory-walk write (one signal) -> log shows 'Embed drain pass finished for Code: 7 row(s)' (the FIRST pass, capped exactly at the configured 7), followed by the periodic code-reindex maintenance job finding the 3 remainder and firing a second signal -> 'Embed drain pass finished for Code: 3 row(s)' (7+3=10, all drained). Across this entire log: EventId 1006 (invalid rows-per-run) never appears anywhere -- the setting stayed valid throughout.
items.observed-result: Both corpora drain fully via the async EmbedDrainService, with zero inline embedding on the write path (source-confirmed: embedInline was removed entirely in PR #518). The rows-per-run cap is honored exactly: a single pass embeds precisely 7 rows when 10 are pending, never more, with the remainder requiring a second signal -- exactly the outbox/pacing design intent. 1006 correctly never fires with the valid setting in place throughout.
items.acceptance-reason: The single-drain-pass-embeds-exactly-7 claim is the strongest evidence in this item: the log line reads 'Embed drain pass finished for Code: 7 row(s)' immediately after a 10-row batch write, followed by a second, separate pass for the remaining 3 -- this could not happen if rows-per-run were ignored or if inline embedding still existed (which would show all 10 embedded before any drain-pass log ever appeared, or no drain-pass logs at all).

items.expected-result: Adding a .cs file under a watch shows the code corpus gets a drain signal (EventId 1002 with corpus Code) -- PR #518 fixed this path (the digest used to unconditionally signal Memory regardless of which corpus a write actually landed in).
items.command: Register a watch on a fresh directory (watch-code-src, code engine active) ; add a new .cs file (WatchedFile.cs) under it ; wait for the watch poll/digest ; check memory_watch_status (lastSync) and memory_search kind=code for the new file's content ; server log grep for EmbedDrainService[1002/1003] immediately following the watch digest's write-lock log line
items.evidence: memory_watch_status showed a fresh lastSync after the file was added. kind=code search found WatchedFile.cs ranked #1 (embedded, not just FTS). Server log (flushed on clean shutdown), in order: 'AiRaccoon.Infrastructure.Sqlite.Memory.SqliteMemoryStore[899] Replace-by-path transaction held the write lock for 4.5 ms (1 row(s) written)' (the watch digest's own write) immediately followed by 'AiRaccoon.Infrastructure.Embedding.EmbedDrainService[1003] Embed drain pass finished for Code: 1 row(s)' -- corpus=Code, not Memory. Read PR #518's own commit (a52b00dd, 'fix(watch): the digest signals the corpus the replace actually wrote to, not always Memory'): the fix replaced IMemoryStore.ReplaceIfFileChangedAsync's bare bool return with ReplaceResult(bool Replaced, CorpusKind Corpus), and WatchDigestExecutor.DigestAsync now enqueues per that corpus instead of unconditionally enqueuing EmbedCorpus.Memory.
items.observed-result: The watched .cs file's write correctly signals and drains the Code corpus (evidenced by the paired 1003 'finished for Code' line, not 'finished for Memory'), matching PR #518's fix. EventId 1002 itself (the 'pass started' line, logged at Debug level) was not directly observable: this build ships no appsettings.json, offers no --log-level CLI flag, and setting the standard ASP.NET Core Logging__LogLevel__Default environment variable had no effect on the console provider's minimum level (confirmed: after a clean restart with that env var set, every subsequent log line, including ones known to exist at Debug level in test coverage, still printed only at Information or above) -- there is no supported way in this build to lower the console log threshold below Information. 1003 for the same drain pass is the adjacent, unconditional log line in the same code path (DrainOnceAsync logs 1002 as its first line and 1003 as its last, with no branch in between) and is Information-level, so its corpus value is conclusive proof the paired 1002 also fired with corpus=Code.
items.acceptance-reason: EventId 1002 itself could not be directly captured live (Debug-level, and this build exposes no supported way to lower the console minimum log level -- confirmed by testing the standard Logging__LogLevel__Default env var, which had no effect). Substituted with EventId 1003 for the same drain pass (unconditionally logged immediately after 1002 in DrainOnceAsync, same corpus value, Information level) plus a read of PR #518's own diff, which is conclusive for the behavior under test (correct corpus routing) even though the specific event id named in the task could not be observed at this build's log level.
